body.html: Big Elephant Hotel — the Thai sign reads Chang Yai Jai Dee — is a 50-room hotel on Liang Mueang Road in Mueang Yasothon. Its single clearest selling point is the location, right behind the Yasothon bus terminal. Anyone who travels by coach in and out of town knows how much that's worth: you step off the bus, roll your bag across the road, and you're at your room — no second ride, no extra fare, no waiting around.

Rooms are simple but cover what you actually need — a comfortable bed, cold AC, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi. Reviews agree the housekeeping is solid: clean rooms, clean floors, and a mattress that's soft in just the right way, which hotels at this price in provincial towns often can't keep consistent. There are single rooms, twin rooms, and slightly larger garden rooms with a king bed, so you can pick by group size and budget.
"Great bed, clean room, everything you need, better than the price — and it's right next to the bus station, so you step off and walk straight in."

Beyond the location, guests often praise the large free parking and the EV charger (AC type) on site. That's a real plus for anyone driving an electric car upcountry, since chargers are still scarce in smaller towns like Yasothon. There's a front garden to sit in, a 24-hour front desk, and paid laundry service. Shops and a massage place are within walking distance, while breakfast isn't included — you'll head out to eat.

Being right behind the bus terminal also makes onward travel easy — the town center, the historic Ban Singha Tha old quarter and the Toad Museum (Phaya Khan Khak) are all a short 7–8 minute drive away. Phaya Thaen Park and the river aren't far either. During the Yasothon Rocket Festival (Bun Bang Fai, in May), a spot this close to the bus terminal fills up fast because so many people arrive by coach for the event. Outside festival season the town is fairly quiet, which many guests count as a plus if you just want to sleep.

To be straight with you, Big Elephant Hotel isn't for everyone. The thing reviewers consistently flag is sound — the walls don't block noise well, and you can sometimes hear talking from the next room or the adjoining balcony. A few reviews mention an older AC unit being a bit loud, and some bathrooms don't fully separate the wet and dry areas. There's no elevator, no pool or spa, and no breakfast. But if the brief is a clean, cheap room right by the coaches, this delivers it in full and the value is real.

In short, Big Elephant Hotel suits coach travelers, road-trippers, business travelers and EV drivers who want a clean, affordable room right by the bus terminal. Real guest reviews consistently score it high for value and cleanliness. If you're a light sleeper, pack earplugs for the noise, and if you're visiting for the Rocket Festival, book several weeks ahead.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Big Elephant Hotel Yasothon

faq.q: Where is Big Elephant Hotel in Yasothon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Big Elephant Hotel is at 468/25 Liang Mueang Road, Nai Mueang, right behind the Yasothon bus terminal. You just walk across the road to the coaches. The town center, the historic Ban Singha Tha old quarter and the Toad Museum are a short 7–8 minute drive away.

faq.q: What does Big Elephant Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿620/night for a Standard single. Twin rooms and the larger king garden rooms run roughly ฿720–฿850. Prices depend on dates and availability — they rise and sell out fast around the Rocket Festival, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Big Elephant Hotel convenient for coach travel?
faq.a: Very. The hotel sits right behind the Yasothon bus terminal — you walk across the road to the coaches. It's ideal for anyone traveling in and out of town by bus: step off, roll your bag straight to your room, no second ride needed.

faq.q: Does Big Elephant Hotel have parking and an EV charger?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's large free parking out front and an on-site EV charger (AC type). That's handy for electric-car drivers upcountry, since chargers are still scarce in smaller towns. It's worth telling the hotel at booking that you'll use the charger.

faq.q: Is Big Elephant Hotel noisy? Will I sleep well?
faq.a: Rooms are clean, the AC is cold and the beds are comfortable, but the walls don't block sound well, so you can sometimes hear talking from the next room or the adjoining balcony. If you're a light sleeper, pack earplugs and ask for a room away from the shared corridor at check-in.

faq.q: Who is Big Elephant Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for coach travelers, road-trippers, business travelers and EV drivers who want a clean, affordable room right by the bus terminal. Real reviews consistently praise the value and cleanliness. It's less suited to anyone wanting breakfast, an elevator, a pool or a spa.
